text.p: Brokers said they were optimistic on Wednesday, as high expectations for Hermis Bank and Baltic Shipyard shares lifted spirits lowered by suspensions of some of the most popular shares on Lithuania's stock exchange.
"It seems that the market is recovering," said Saulius Merkys, a broker with Vilfima.
"The mood is positive," said Tomas Andrejauskas, a broker with Suprema.
"We had six ups, four downs and seven shares stayed at the same level as yesterday," Andrejauskas said.

"Probably we'll see some interesting things in the next one or two months with Lithuanian Sea Shipping Company (LISCO), Ekranas, Hermis Bank, Rokishkis Cheese and Vilniaus Vingis going up," Merkys said.
Hermis Bank advanced to 180.00 litas from 175.00 litas, while Rokishkis held steady at 44.00 litas.
Trading in Vilniaus Vingis was suspended today, as were Vilniaus Bank shares. The Lithuanian bourse is weathering a number of suspensions for shareholders' meetings and other business.
Ekranas shares edged up slightly to 5.31 litas from 5.29 litas. LISCO was at 6.55 litas from 6.52 litas.

Baltic Shipyard shares were also raised to 8.31 litas from 8.12 litas on news the government was planning to sell the state's 11.26 million litas stake on the bourse between June 7 and August 7, brokers said.
